y1: The Pharisees considered picking grain as 'reaping' and rubbing it as 'threshing,' calling this a violation of the Sabbath. The rabbis had divided forbidden work into 39 categories.
y2: Jesus gives the example of David eating the consecrated bread and the priests who work on the Sabbath. Then He declares: “One greater than the temple is here,” and “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
y3: The Sabbath controversy comes immediately after the words “I will give you rest.” True rest is found in Jesus, not in rules. Following 9:13, Jesus again recalls Hosea 6:6 (“I desire mercy, and not sacrifice”).
y4: It is lawful to do good
y5: Looking for a reason to accuse Him, the Pharisees asked, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” According to the rules of that time, if a life was not in danger, medical treatment had to be postponed to the next day.
y6: Jesus gave the example of a sheep falling into a pit and said, “It is lawful to do good on the Sabbath,” and He healed the hand. But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus. Jesus, who gives life on the Sabbath, is contrasted with those who plot to kill on the Sabbath.
y7: Rules exist to keep people alive. If we lose the person while keeping the rule, we have lost the purpose of the rule. Jesus didn't break the Law; He restored the heart of the Law (5:17).
y9: Matthew quotes at length from Isaiah 42:1–4: “He will not quarrel nor cry out... A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not snuff out, till He leads justice to victory. In His name the nations will put their hope.”
y10: But the Pharisees called Jesus's driving out of demons the power of Beelzebul. Jesus said, “Make a tree good and its fruit will be good,” explaining that the mouth speaks what the heart is full of. On the day of judgment, people will have to give an account for every empty word.
y11: The “blasphemy against the Holy Spirit” in 12:31–32 is not an accidental slip of the tongue. It is a heart that sees the clear work of the Holy Spirit, deliberately calls it evil, and rejects it to the end. A person who is worried about committing this is already not in that state.
y12: The sign of Jonah and the new family
y13: When the people ask for a sign, Jesus says: “No sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.” Just as Jonah was in the belly of the huge fish for three days, the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days. This is the first announcement of the resurrection.
y14: When His mother and brothers arrive, Jesus points to His disciples and says: “Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.” It is a new family bound not by blood, but by obedience.
y15: Even on the cross, Jesus entrusted His mother to John (John 19:26–27). He didn't neglect His family; He showed that the family of the kingdom of heaven is much broader. Anyone who feels like an orphan can enter this family.
verse: “A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not snuff out, till He leads justice to victory. In His name the nations will put their hope.”
prayer: Jesus, Lord of the Sabbath, thank You for being the one who gives rest and life, not rules. Do not break me when I am like a bruised reed, and rekindle my smoldering faith. Let me live as Your family, doing the Father's will. I pray in Jesus Christ's name. Amen.
d0: Sabbath. The book of Exodus tells us to remember creation, and Deuteronomy tells us to remember freedom from slavery in Egypt (Deut. 5:15). A slave cannot rest, but God's people rest. The early church celebrated the day Jesus rose (Sunday) as the 'Lord's Day'.
d1: reed. A reed breaks easily, and a cracked reed was considered useless and thrown away. Jesus doesn't even break that. He doesn't blow out a smoldering wick either, but rekindles it.
d2: Beelzebul. It was originally the name of a Philistine idol (2 Kings 1:2), but the Jews used this name to mock Satan. Jesus showed the contradiction of this logic by saying, “A kingdom divided against itself will be ruined.”
d3: family. The early believers called each other 'brother' and 'sister'. It is a family bound by Jesus, not by blood. In our churches too, we call each other 'brother' and 'sister'.
